llm.reply:
The retrieved records cover two mismatch repair genes and a set of hereditary cancer syndromes, but they do not show which syndrome is linked to which gene, so a direct comparison of their colorectal cancer risk is not possible from these records. The first gene is NCBIGene:4292 [1]. The second gene is NCBIGene:4436 [5].

## Genes Retrieved

NCBIGene:4292 is named mutL homolog 1 [1]. NCBIGene:4436 is named mutS homolog 2 [5]. The gene symbol recorded for NCBIGene:4292 is MLH1 [8].

## Associated Syndromes

One retrieved condition is Lynch syndrome 1 [6]. Another is Colorectal cancer, hereditary nonpolyposis, type 2 [3]. Another is Muir-TorrÃ© syndrome [2]. Another is Mismatch repair cancer syndrome 1 [4]. Another is Mismatch repair cancer syndrome 2 [7]. The findings do not assign these conditions to either gene individually.

## MLH1 Function

The MLH1 protein pairs with PMS2 to form part of the mismatch repair machinery [18: "heterodimerize with mismatch repair endonuclease PMS2 to form MutL alpha, part of the DNA mismatch repair system"]. It is frequently mutated in inherited colon cancer [18: "identified as a locus frequently mutated in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (HNPCC)"]. One study developed a functional test for uncertain variants in both genes [27: "Functional Assay to Assess Variants of Unknown Significance in the MLH1 and MSH2 Genes and Identify Patients With Lynch Syndrome"].

It also includes Mismatch repair cancer syndrome 2 [7]. The records do not specify which gene each condition belongs to, so they do not support a direct comparison of risk between the two genes.

## MLH1 Function

The gene symbol is MLH1 [8]. The gene name is MLH1 [12]. The OMIM entry is DNA MISMATCH REPAIR PROTEIN MLH1; MLH1 [11]. Its product works with PMS2 in DNA mismatch repair [18: "heterodimerize with mismatch repair endonuclease PMS2 to form MutL alpha, part of the DNA mismatch repair system"], and the gene is often mutated in hereditary colon cancer [18: "identified as a locus frequently mutated in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (HNPCC)"]. Annotated processes include GO:0006298, name: mismatch repair [21]. They also include GO:0000710, name: meiotic mismatch repair [15]. Another is GO:0006950, name: response to stress [26].

## Variants and Literature

One ClinVar variant is NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.545+1271_677+737delinsCA [10]. Another is NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.453+625_545+920delinsT [17]. Another is NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.1418A>T (p.His473Leu) [23]. Another is NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.884+5T>A [28]. One paper is Functional analysis of human MLH1 variants using yeast and in vitro mismatch repair assays. [9] Another is Coexisting somatic promoter hypermethylation and pathogenic MLH1 germline mutation in Lynch syndrome. [16] Another is Novel 2-Benzoyl-6-(2,3-Dimethoxybenzylidene)-Cyclohexenol Confers Selectivity toward Human MLH1 Defective Cancer Cells through Synthetic Lethality. [22] One functional assay paper covers both genes, titled Methylation Tolerance-Based Functional Assay to Assess Variants of Unknown Significance in the MLH1 and MSH2 Genes and Identify Patients With Lynch Syndrome. [27] Related publications include PMID 17510385 [14]. Another is PMID 17973250 [20]. Another is PMID 30897027 [25]. Another is PMID 30998989 [30].

## Clinical Trials

One trial is The IMPACT Study - Identification of Men With a Genetic Predisposition to ProstAte Cancer [13]. Another is Study of MK-3475 in Patients With Microsatellite Unstable (MSI) Tumors (Cohorts A, B and C) [19]. Another is Surgery in Preventing Ovarian Cancer in Patients With Genetic Mutations [24]. Another is Stand up to Cancer: MAGENTA (Making Genetic Testing Accessible) [29].
